units.title: Sophie Germain factorization in a prime-power divisibility problem
units.statement: For prime p and odd positive m,k, suppose m⁴+4^k p⁴ divides m²(m⁴−4^k p⁴). If p∤m, the divisor is coprime to m and would divide both m⁴+4^k p⁴ and m⁴−4^k p⁴, hence divide 2m⁴, impossible. Write m=p^t u with p∤u. Cancelling p⁴ and reducing modulo A=p^(4t−4)u⁴+4^k gives A|p^(2t), because A is coprime to 2u. For t≥2, p∤A, impossible. Thus t=1 and A=u⁴+4^k is p or p². Since k is odd, put v=2^((k−1)/2) and factor A=(u²−2uv+2v²)(u²+2uv+2v²). The factors are unequal positive integers, so the smaller must be 1; (u−v)²+v²=1 forces u=v=1, k=1, p=5, m=5. Direct substitution gives quotient −15.
steps: Show p divides m and cancel its fourth power
Reduce the quotient condition to a small p-power
Apply Sophie Germain's identity and inspect the smaller factor
